Kofun |Icon=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is designated as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also designated as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not designated as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of platforms, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, designated on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == Aerial view of Shiroyama Kofun (circa 1961). The arrangement of surrounding residential buildings reveals the presence of an outer moat.{{Aerial Photography of Japan}} |part_of={{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} |location=[[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, Tsudo |coordinatess=34|coordinatess=34|coordinatess=55.26 |coordinatess=135|coordinatess=35|coordinatess=36.33 |omitted=JP-27 |type={{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area= Mound length 208m
Height 16.9m |built= Late 4th century (~370 CE{{Cite book |author={{ill|Amano Suemasa|ja|天野末喜}} |title=Considering Imperial Tomb Kofun and the Buried Figures |publisher=Yosensha |year=2016 |pages=60–63}}[https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/koramukodaikaranomemessezi/wanogoozidai/10289.html built of Large Kofun 1 (No. 162)], Fujidera City Homepage.) |burial={{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}}
(with {{ill|Coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}-designated "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |other_designation= National other_designation "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is designated as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also designated as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not designated as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of platforms, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, designated on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is designated as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designated it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also designated as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not designated as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of platforms, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are designated as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, designated on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of platforms, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * (Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of platforms, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} (Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of platforms, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Aerial view of Shiroyama Kofun (circa 1961). The arrangement of surrounding residential buildings reveals the presence of an outer moat.{{Aerial Photography of Japan}} |part_of={{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} |location=[[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, Tsudo |coordinates=34|coordinates=34|coordinates=55.26 |coordinates=135|coordinates=35|coordinates=36.33 |omitted=JP-27 |type={{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area= Mound length 208m
Height 16.9m |built= Late 4th century (~370 CE{{Cite book |author={{ill|Amano Suemasa|ja|天野末喜}} |title=Considering Imperial Tomb Kofun and the Buried Figures |publisher=Yosensha |year=2016 |pages=60–63}}[https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/koramukodaikaranomemessezi/wanogoozidai/10289.html built of Large Kofun 1 (No. 162)], Fujidera City Homepage.) |burial={{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}}
(with {{ill|Coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}-other_designation1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |other_designation= National other_designation "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Aerial view of Shiroyama Kofun (circa 1961). The arrangement of surrounding residential buildings reveals the presence of an outer moat.{{Aerial Photography of Japan}} |part_of={{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} |location=[[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, Tsudo |coordinates=34|coordinates=34|coordinates=55.26 |coordinates=135|coordinates=35|coordinates=36.33 |omitted=JP-27 |type={{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |area= Mound length 208m
Height 16.9m |built= Late 4th century (~370 CE{{Cite book |author={{ill|Amano Suemasa|ja|天野末喜}} |title=Considering Imperial Tomb Kofun and the Buried Figures |publisher=Yosensha |year=2016 |pages=60–63}}[https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/koramukodaikaranomemessezi/wanogoozidai/10289.html built of Large Kofun 1 (No. 162)], Fujidera City Homepage.) |burial={{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber}}
(with {{ill|Coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}) 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}-other_designation1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |other_designation= National other_designation "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating Burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} (Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}}-other_designation1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |other_designation= National other_designation "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{other_designationDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National other_designation === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}" other_designation, other_designation1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{other_designationDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}, which is other_designation1 as a {{ill|World other_designation Site|ja|文化遺産}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} has other_designation1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇}}. The kofun is also other_designation1 as a National other_designation (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代}}, the kofun was not other_designation1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent other_designation as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the other_designation of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun Period*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural Designation == === National Important Cultural Property === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are other_designation1 as [[Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall}}.
