While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|12=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[Important designation1 (Japan)|Important designation1]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft}}. (with {{ill|Coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}) 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft}}
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=draft}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}}-Historic Site1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |Historic Site= National Historic Site "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|12=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|12=draft}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|12=draft}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|12=draft}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo (Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, *Imperial Tombs*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft|12=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|12=draft|12=draft}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|12=draft|12=draft}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} of Osaka Prefecture]] {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujidera City]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Mausoleum reference sites]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Ingyō Tennō]] [[Category:Tsudō Shiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] }} [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[sn:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[en:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]]

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft|12=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|12=draft|12=draft}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|12=draft|12=draft}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} of Osaka Prefecture]] {{draft categories| }} {{citation needed|Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujidera City]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Mausoleum reference sites]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Ingyō Tennō]] [[Category:Tsudō Shiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]][[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[sn:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[en:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]]

(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|Aisell Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft|12=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * Aerial view of Shiroyama Kofun (circa 1961). The arrangement of surrounding residential buildings reveals the presence of an outer moat.{{Aerial Photography of Japan}} |part_of={{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} |location=[[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]], {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Tsudo |coordinates=34|coordinates=34|coordinates=55.26 |coordinates=135|coordinates=35|coordinates=36.33 |omitted=JP-27 |type={{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} |area= Mound length 208m
Height 16.9m |built= Late 4th century (~370 CE{{Cite book |author={{ill|Amano Suemasa|ja|天野末喜|12=draft|12=draft}} |title=Considering Mausoleum Kofun and the Interred_individuals |publisher=Yosensha |year=2016 |pages=60–63}}[https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/koramukodaikaranomemessezi/wanogoozidai/10289.html built of Large Kofun 1 (No. 162)], Fujidera City Homepage.) |burial={{ill|Vertical stone chamber|ja|竪穴式石室|1=Vertical Pit-Style Stone Chamber|12=draft|12=draft}}
(with {{ill|Coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}) 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=draft|12=draft}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}-Historic Site1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |Historic Site= National Historic Site "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft|12=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|12=draft|12=draft}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|12=draft|12=draft}} to Koyama or Taisho (with {{ill|Coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}) 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=draft|12=draft}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}}-Historic Site1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |Historic Site= National Historic Site "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|12=draft|12=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|12=draft|12=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|12=draft|12=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|12=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=draft|12=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|12=draft|12=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * (with {{ill|Coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-Historic Site1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |Historic Site= National Historic Site "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * (Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|qq=draft|qq=draft}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum={{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}-Historic Site1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |Historic Site= National Historic Site "Shiroyama Kofun"
(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic {{日本の古墳 |名称= 津堂城山古墳 |画像= [[画像:610530 T Shiroyama Kofun aerial.jpg|250px]]
上空から見た城山古墳（1961年当時）。古墳周囲の住宅の並び方で外側周濠の存在がわかる。{{国土航空写真}} |所属=[[古市古墳群]] |所在地= [[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]津堂 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 34|緯度秒 = 55.26 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 35|経度秒 = 36.33 |ISO = JP-27 |形状= [[前方後円墳]] |規模= 墳丘長208m
高さ16.9m |築造年代= [[4世紀]]後半(370年頃[[天野末喜]] 「天皇陵古墳と被葬者を考える」『古代史研究の最前線 天皇陵』 洋泉社、2016年、pp. 60 - 63。[https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/koramukodaikaranomemessezi/wanogoozidai/10289.html　巨大古墳の築造年代1(No.162)]　藤井寺市ホームページ) |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]]
（内部に[[長持形石棺]]） |被葬者=（[[宮内庁]]推定）第19代[[允恭天皇]]
（一説）[[日本武尊]] |出土品= 埴輪・銅鏡・玉類・鉄鏃等 |陵墓=[[宮内庁]]治定「藤井寺陵墓参考地」 |史跡=国の[[史跡]]「城山古墳」
（「古市古墳群」に包含） |特記事項=全国第31位の規模[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html 古墳大きさランキング（日本全国版）]（堺市ホームページ、2018年5月13日更新版）。 |地図 = Japan Osaka |ラベル = 津堂城山
古墳 |アイコン = 前方後円墳-南東 }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|藤井寺陵墓参考地 立札}}]] '''津堂城山古墳'''（つどうしろやまこふん）は、[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。[[古市古墳群]]（[[文化遺産 (世界遺産)|世界文化遺産]]）を構成する古墳の1つ。 実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]により「'''藤井寺陵墓参考地'''」（被葬候補者：第19代[[允恭天皇]]）として[[陵墓参考地]]に治定されている。また国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「古市古墳群」のうち）。 == 概要 == 前方部は南東を向き、二重の周濠が墳丘を囲んでいる。外側の周濠は宅地や田畑となっているが、これを含めると古墳の全長は400[[メートル|m]]以上になる。 これまでの発掘調査などから築造は4世紀後半とみられ、古市古墳群の中でも初期の古墳であり、[[誉田山古墳]]よりも先行する。[[室町時代]]には古墳の地形を利用して小山城が築かれたため、墳丘の一部が掘削されている。明治初期の天皇陵の治定作業では陵墓とされなかったが、1912年に、神社に建立する石碑の材料とするため、後円部の墳丘から石板を発掘したことがきっかけで竪穴式石室と巨大な[[長持形石棺]]が発見され、鏡や鏃などの副葬品が多数出土した。そのため、後に「藤井寺[[陵墓参考地]]」に治定された。 [[1980年]]に大阪府教育委員会が、[[1983年]]には藤井寺市教育委員会が発掘調査を実施。[[造り出し]]や二重の周濠（中堤幅30m、外濠25m）、石葺の外側堤（幅20m）の存在が確認された。また、周濠内の前方部左右近くの島状遺構（方墳形の祭壇）からは3体の水鳥形[[埴輪]]が出土。このほかにも衝立型や家形・盾形・衣蓋形、靫型の埴輪、円筒型など多彩な形象埴輪が発見された。 これらの内、複数の周濠や堤などの建築様式は[[誉田御廟山古墳]]や[[大仙古墳]]をはじめとする5世紀以降の大王墳の基本形態として継承されており、本古墳はその起源と見なすことができる事から大和から河内へと古墳築造が移った初期の大王の陵墓ではないかと考えられている[[天野末喜]] 「天皇陵古墳と被葬者を考える」『古代史研究の最前線 天皇陵』 洋泉社、2016年、p.64。しかし同時期に墳丘単体の規模で当古墳を大きく上回る[[五社神古墳]]が佐紀の地に築かれている事や、馬見地域で築山古墳や[[巣山古墳]]といった同等規模の古墳が多数営まれている事などを踏まえ、大王墳と見なすのは難しいとする説もある[[清家章]] 『埋葬からみた古墳時代』 吉川弘文館、2018年、p.206[[矢澤高太郎]] 『天皇陵』 中央公論新社、2012年、p.109。 [[1958年]][[1月21日]]に国の史跡に指定。[[2001年]][[1月29日]]には、個々の古墳の指定を統合した古市古墳群全体として史跡に指定されている。 ===　被葬者　=== 大王墳とする説を支持し、尚且つ記紀の内容を重視する立場の研究者の何名かは、初めて河内に埋葬された大王として記述された[[仲哀天皇]]を被葬者の候補として提案している[[矢澤高太郎]] 『天皇陵』 中央公論新社、2012年、p.106[[矢澤高太郎]] 『天皇陵』 中央公論新社、2012年、p.109[[藤井利章]] 「津堂城山古墳の研究」『藤井寺市史紀要』　藤井寺市　1982年。 [[森浩一]]は古墳から出土した水鳥形埴輪と記紀の伝承との間に関連を見て、仲哀天皇の父で死後に白鳥となって天に昇ったとされる[[ヤマトタケル]]の三つの墓の一つである可能性を指摘した[[森浩一]] 『天皇陵の謎』 筑摩書房、2011年、p.124 - p.125[[森浩一]] 『天皇陵の謎』 筑摩書房、2011年、p.132 - p.133。また、古墳の築造者としては仲哀天皇の息子で神功皇后と誉田別皇子([[応神天皇]])に対して反乱を起こした[[忍熊王]]を挙げている[[森浩一]] 『天皇陵の謎』 筑摩書房、2011年、p.196 - p.202。宮内庁は[[軽里大塚古墳]]を記紀に語られたヤマトタケルの墓に定めているものの、考古学上の編年では5世紀後半の築造であると推定されているため、それよりも1世紀ほど年代が古く、尚且つヤマトタケルの父である[[景行天皇]]の陵とされる[[渋谷向山古墳]]の築造年代とも近接する本古墳の方が伝承にある墓として相応しいと考えられる。 豪族間での王権移動を重視する立場からは応神天皇の妃の父として記される品陀真若王の名が挙げられる。塚口義信は津堂城山古墳を王権の中枢が河内に移動する直前にその一帯の中小豪族を束ね、後に外戚として誉田別尊の一族と結びついて王権を掌握する礎となった大豪族の墓と考えており、品陀真若はこうした豪族間の繋がりが天皇家の系譜へと整理される中で一人の皇族という形に反映された姿と捉える[[塚口義信]] 『ヤマト王権の謎をとく』 学生社、1993年、p.117-p.121。また、品陀真若王は系図上[[景行天皇]]の孫にも相当するため、河内の勢力が4世紀前半に王権を握っていた三輪山周辺の勢力とも繋がりを有していた可能性も指摘している[[塚口義信]] 『ヤマト王権の謎をとく』 学生社、1993年、p.122-p.127。 == 構造 == [[File:Shiroyama_kofun.png|thumb|250px|right|{{center|1985年当時の空中写真}}{{small|{{国土航空写真}}}}]] [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}{{small|右に前方部、左奥に後円部。}}]] * 墳丘長208m * 前方部 - 幅117m、高さ12.7m * 後円部 - 径128m、高さ16.9m File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-1.jpg|前方部から後円部を望む File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|後円部から前方部を望む File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, tenjouishi.jpg|竪穴式石室天井石
{{small|史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」展示。}} == 主な出土品 == * 水鳥形埴輪 3点（国の[[重要文化財]]） ** 4世紀ごろ。藤井寺市が所有。[[アイセルシュラホール]]で展示。 * 鰭付円筒埴輪 ** 4世紀ごろ。大阪府教育委員会が所有。[[大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館]]で展示。 * さしば形埴輪 ** 4世紀ごろ。大阪府教育委員会が所有。大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館で展示。 File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, sekkan.jpg|長持形石棺（複製）
{{small|史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」展示。}} ファイル:津堂城山古墳出土 形象埴輪.JPG|形象埴輪
{{small|手前の水鳥形埴輪3点は国の[[重要文化財]]。[[アイセルシュラホール|藤井寺市立生涯学習センター（アイセル シュラ ホール）]]展示。}} ファイル:津堂城山古墳出土 衝立形埴輪.JPG|衝立形埴輪
{{small|史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」展示。}} == 施設など == 周濠を通って墳丘へと至る道筋はいくつかあり、自由に立ち入ることができるため、古くから子供の遊び場や近隣の人々の憩いの場となっている。ただし、後円部墳丘の頂上部は金網で囲まれ、宮内庁が陵墓参考地として管理しているため立ち入ることができない。 ; 史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」 : 後円部北にある展示施設。入館無料。 ; 津堂八幡神社 : 後円部の北側中腹にある。当社にある石碑は、後円部から掘り出した石板で竪穴式石室の一部（天井部分）とされる。 ; 花しょうぶ園 : [[大阪府道186号大阪羽曳野線|府道大阪羽曳野線]]に面した東側の周濠約4,000[[平方メートル|m2]]に[[ハナショウブ]]や[[スイレン属|スイレン]]などが植えられている。[[1991年]]4月に完成。 ; 津堂草花園 : [[1998年]]4月に古墳北側の集合部分に完成。約4,000m2。 {{multiple image | align = left | image1 = Tsudo-hachiman-jinja, haiden.jpg | width1 = 200 | caption1 =
津堂八幡神社
| image2 = Shiroyama_kofun02.png | width2 = 200 | caption2 =
花しょうぶ園と墳丘部

津堂草花園

{{日本の古墳 |名称= 津堂城山古墳 |画像= [[画像:610530 T Shiroyama Kofun aerial.jpg|250px]]
上空から見た城山古墳（1961年当時）。古墳周囲の住宅の並び方で外側周濠の存在がわかる。{{国土航空写真}} |所属=[[古市古墳群]] |所在地= [[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]津堂 |緯度度 = 34|緯度分 = 34|緯度秒 = 55.26 |経度度 =135|経度分 = 35|経度秒 = 36.33 |ISO = JP-27 |形状= [[前方後円墳]] |規模= 墳丘長208m
高さ16.9m |築造年代= [[4世紀]]後半(370年頃[[天野末喜]] 「天皇陵古墳と被葬者を考える」『古代史研究の最前線 天皇陵』 洋泉社、2016年、pp. 60 - 63。[https://www.city.fujiidera.lg.jp/soshiki/kyoikuiinkai/bunkazaihogo/koramukodaikaranomemessezi/wanogoozidai/10289.html　巨大古墳の築造年代1(No.162)]　藤井寺市ホームページ) |埋葬施設=[[竪穴式石室]]
（内部に[[長持形石棺]]） |被葬者=（[[宮内庁]]推定）第19代[[允恭天皇]]
（一説）[[日本武尊]] |出土品= 埴輪・銅鏡・玉類・鉄鏃等 |陵墓=[[宮内庁]]治定「藤井寺陵墓参考地」 |史跡=国の[[史跡]]「城山古墳」
（「古市古墳群」に包含） |特記事項=全国第31位の規模[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html 古墳大きさランキング（日本全国版）]（堺市ホームページ、2018年5月13日更新版）。 |地図 = Japan Osaka |ラベル = 津堂城山
古墳 |アイコン = 前方後円墳-南東 }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|藤井寺陵墓参考地 立札}}]] '''津堂城山古墳'''（つどうしろやまこふん）は、[[大阪府]][[藤井寺市]]にある[[古墳]]。形状は[[前方後円墳]]。[[古市古墳群]]（[[文化遺産 (世界遺産)|世界文化遺産]]）を構成する古墳の1つ。 実際の被葬者は明らかでないが、[[宮内庁]]により「'''藤井寺陵墓参考地'''」（被葬候補者：第19代[[允恭天皇]]）として[[陵墓参考地]]に治定されている。また国の[[史跡]]に指定されている（史跡「古市古墳群」のうち）。 == 概要 == 前方部は南東を向き、二重の周濠が墳丘を囲んでいる。外側の周濠は宅地や田畑となっているが、これを含めると古墳の全長は400[[メートル|m]]以上になる。 これまでの発掘調査などから築造は4世紀後半とみられ、古市古墳群の中でも初期の古墳であり、[[誉田山古墳]]よりも先行する。[[室町時代]]には古墳の地形を利用して小山城が築かれたため、墳丘の一部が掘削されている。明治初期の天皇陵の治定作業では陵墓とされなかったが、1912年に、神社に建立する石碑の材料とするため、後円部の墳丘から石板を発掘したことがきっかけで竪穴式石室と巨大な[[長持形石棺]]が発見され、鏡や鏃などの副葬品が多数出土した。そのため、後に「藤井寺[[陵墓参考地]]」に治定された。 [[1980年]]に大阪府教育委員会が、[[1983年]]には藤井寺市教育委員会が発掘調査を実施。[[造り出し]]や二重の周濠（中堤幅30m、外濠25m）、石葺の外側堤（幅20m）の存在が確認された。また、周濠内の前方部左右近くの島状遺構（方墳形の祭壇）からは3体の水鳥形[[埴輪]]が出土。このほかにも衝立型や家形・盾形・衣蓋形、靫型の埴輪、円筒型など多彩な形象埴輪が発見された。 これらの内、複数の周濠や堤などの建築様式は[[誉田御廟山古墳]]や[[大仙古墳]]をはじめとする5世紀以降の大王墳の基本形態として継承されており、本古墳はその起源と見なすことができる事から大和から河内へと古墳築造が移った初期の大王の陵墓ではないかと考えられている[[天野末喜]] 「天皇陵古墳と被葬者を考える」『古代史研究の最前線 天皇陵』 洋泉社、2016年、p.64。しかし同時期に墳丘単体の規模で当古墳を大きく上回る[[五社神古墳]]が佐紀の地に築かれている事や、馬見地域で築山古墳や[[巣山古墳]]といった同等規模の古墳が多数営まれている事などを踏まえ、大王墳と見なすのは難しいとする説もある[[清家章]] 『埋葬からみた古墳時代』 吉川弘文館、2018年、p.206[[矢澤高太郎]] 『天皇陵』 中央公論新社、2012年、p.109。 [[1958年]][[1月21日]]に国の史跡に指定。[[2001年]][[1月29日]]には、個々の古墳の指定を統合した古市古墳群全体として史跡に指定されている。 ===　被葬者　=== 大王墳とする説を支持し、尚且つ記紀の内容を重視する立場の研究者の何名かは、初めて河内に埋葬された大王として記述された[[仲哀天皇]]を被葬者の候補として提案している[[矢澤高太郎]] 『天皇陵』 中央公論新社、2012年、p.106[[矢澤高太郎]] 『天皇陵』 中央公論新社、2012年、p.109[[藤井利章]] 「津堂城山古墳の研究」『藤井寺市史紀要』　藤井寺市　1982年。 [[森浩一]]は古墳から出土した水鳥形埴輪と記紀の伝承との間に関連を見て、仲哀天皇の父で死後に白鳥となって天に昇ったとされる[[ヤマトタケル]]の三つの墓の一つである可能性を指摘した[[森浩一]] 『天皇陵の謎』 筑摩書房、2011年、p.124 - p.125[[森浩一]] 『天皇陵の謎』 筑摩書房、2011年、p.132 - p.133。また、古墳の築造者としては仲哀天皇の息子で神功皇后と誉田別皇子([[応神天皇]])に対して反乱を起こした[[忍熊王]]を挙げている[[森浩一]] 『天皇陵の謎』 筑摩書房、2011年、p.196 - p.202。宮内庁は[[軽里大塚古墳]]を記紀に語られたヤマトタケルの墓に定めているものの、考古学上の編年では5世紀後半の築造であると推定されているため、それよりも1世紀ほど年代が古く、尚且つヤマトタケルの父である[[景行天皇]]の陵とされる[[渋谷向山古墳]]の築造年代とも近接する本古墳の方が伝承にある墓として相応しいと考えられる。 豪族間での王権移動を重視する立場からは応神天皇の妃の父として記される品陀真若王の名が挙げられる。塚口義信は津堂城山古墳を王権の中枢が河内に移動する直前にその一帯の中小豪族を束ね、後に外戚として誉田別尊の一族と結びついて王権を掌握する礎となった大豪族の墓と考えており、品陀真若はこうした豪族間の繋がりが天皇家の系譜へと整理される中で一人の皇族という形に反映された姿と捉える[[塚口義信]] 『ヤマト王権の謎をとく』 学生社、1993年、p.117-p.121。また、品陀真若王は系図上[[景行天皇]]の孫にも相当するため、河内の勢力が4世紀前半に王権を握っていた三輪山周辺の勢力とも繋がりを有していた可能性も指摘している[[塚口義信]] 『ヤマト王権の謎をとく』 学生社、1993年、p.122-p.127。 == 構造 == [[File:Shiroyama_kofun.png|thumb|250px|right|{{center|1985年当時の空中写真}}{{small|{{国土航空写真}}}}]] [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, funkyu-2.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|墳丘}}{{small|右に前方部、左奥に後円部。}}]] * 墳丘長208m * 前方部 - 幅117m、高さ12.7m * 後円部 - 径128m、高さ16.9m File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-1.jpg|前方部から後円部を望む File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, zenpoubu.jpg|後円部から前方部を望む File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, tenjouishi.jpg|竪穴式石室天井石
{{small|史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」展示。}} == 主な出土品 == * 水鳥形埴輪 3点（国の[[重要文化財]]） ** 4世紀ごろ。藤井寺市が所有。[[アイセルシュラホール]]で展示。 * 鰭付円筒埴輪 ** 4世紀ごろ。大阪府教育委員会が所有。[[大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館]]で展示。 * さしば形埴輪 ** 4世紀ごろ。大阪府教育委員会が所有。大阪府立近つ飛鳥博物館で展示。 File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, sekkan.jpg|長持形石棺（複製）
{{small|史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」展示。}} ファイル:津堂城山古墳出土 形象埴輪.JPG|形象埴輪
{{small|手前の水鳥形埴輪3点は国の[[重要文化財]]。[[アイセルシュラホール|藤井寺市立生涯学習センター（アイセル シュラ ホール）]]展示。}} ファイル:津堂城山古墳出土 衝立形埴輪.JPG|衝立形埴輪
{{small|史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」展示。}} == 施設など == 周濠を通って墳丘へと至る道筋はいくつかあり、自由に立ち入ることができるため、古くから子供の遊び場や近隣の人々の憩いの場となっている。ただし、後円部墳丘の頂上部は金網で囲まれ、宮内庁が陵墓参考地として管理しているため立ち入ることができない。 ; 史跡城山古墳ガイダンス棟「まほらしろやま」 : 後円部北にある展示施設。入館無料。 ; 津堂八幡神社 : 後円部の北側中腹にある。当社にある石碑は、後円部から掘り出した石板で竪穴式石室の一部（天井部分）とされる。 ; 花しょうぶ園 : [[大阪府道186号大阪羽曳野線|府道大阪羽曳野線]]に面した東側の周濠約4,000[[平方メートル|m2]]に[[ハナショウブ]]や[[スイレン属|スイレン]]などが植えられている。[[1991年]]4月に完成。 ; 津堂草花園 : [[1998年]]4月に古墳北側の集合部分に完成。約4,000m2。 {{multiple image | align = left | image1 = Tsudo-hachiman-jinja, haiden.jpg | width1 = 200 | caption1 =
津堂八幡神社
| image2 = Shiroyama_kofun02.png | width2 = 200 | caption2 =
花しょうぶ園と墳丘部

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.
