Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujidera City]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Mausoleum reference sites]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Ingyō Tennō]] [[Category:Tsudō Shiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]][[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]]}} [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[sn:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[en:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]]

(Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera City|qq=}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Historic Site Site|qq=}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ingyō Tennō|qq=}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera City|qq=}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Historic Site Site|qq=}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ingyō Tennō|qq=}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisen Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. (Part of "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera City|qq=}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Historic Site Site|qq=}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ingyō Tennō|qq=}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and predating the {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|qq=}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera Station|qq=}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Bus|qq=}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera City|qq=}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Historic Site Site|qq=}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ingyō Tennō|qq=}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera City|qq=}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Historic Site Site|qq=}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ingyō Tennō|qq=}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * {{ill|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|ja|近鉄南大阪線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line|qq=}} {{ill|Fujidera Station|ja|藤井寺駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera Station|qq=}}, followed by a {{ill|Kintetsu Bus|ja|近鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Bus|qq=}} to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} (ancient Kofun) located in {{ill|Fujidera City|ja|藤井寺市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujidera City|qq=}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ja|大阪府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osaka Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/keyhole-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} and part of the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, which is Historic Site1 as a {{ill|World Historic Site Site|ja|文化遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Historic Site Site|qq=}}. While the actual person buried is unknown, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor {{ill|Ingyō Tennō|ja|允恭天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ingyō Tennō|qq=}}. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}}"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the {{ill|Furuichi Kofun Cluster|ja|古市古墳群|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Furuichi Kofun Cluster|qq=}} and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}}, the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early {{ill|Meiji period|ja|明治|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era|2=ja|3=明治|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/haniwa|qq=}}, along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Suzuyama Kofun|ja|巣山古墳|1=Suyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Suyama Kofun|qq=}} in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ja|重要文化財|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|2=ja|3=重要文化財|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|4=ko|5=일본의_중요문화재|lt=Important Cultural Property|qq= (Japan)|ko|일본의_중요문화재|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qq=}} of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "{{ill|Furuichi Kofun The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujidera City]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]][[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]]}} [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[sn:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[en:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:允恭天皇]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Group]] [[Category:大阪府にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:大阪府の重要文化財]]

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Site|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujidera City]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]][[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]]}} [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[sn:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[en:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:允恭天皇]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Group]] [[Category:大阪府にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:大阪府の重要文化財]] [[Category:藤井寺市の歴史]] [[Category:陵墓参考地]]

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it]] [[Category:Kofun template and pages that transclude it 2]] [[Category:marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:Kofun in Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujidera City]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:National Historic Sites of Osaka Prefecture]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]][[Category:Secondary Marked infobox kofun with unknown parameters]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property (Japan)]] [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]][[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]]}} [[sn:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[sn:Tsudoshiroyama Kofun]] [[en:Tsudō-Shiroyama Kofun]] [[Category:允恭天皇]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Group]] [[Category:大阪府にある国指定の史跡]] [[Category:大阪府の古墳]] [[Category:大阪府の重要文化財]] [[Category:藤井寺市の歴史]] [[Category:Candidate Imperial Mausoleums]]

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style stone coffin|ja|長持形石棺|1=Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style stone coffin|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagamochi style stone sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun
