(Part of "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|qid=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11555978}}

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|qq=|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. (with {{ill|Coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]
(Alternative theory) {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} |burial goods= Haniwa, bronze mirrors, jewels, iron arrowheads, etc. |Mausoleum=[[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]-Historic Site1 "Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area" |Historic Site= National Historic Site "Shiroyama Kofun"

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]]

(with {{ill|Coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]]

Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]]

(Part of "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] {{wikidata link|Q11555978}}

Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q11555978}}

Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:pages with conflicting qids]]

(with {{ill|Coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}) |Deceased= (Assumed by [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]]) 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]

(Part of "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]") |Notable= 31st largest kofun in Japan[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas (Japan Nationwide)] (Sakai City Homepage, updated May 13, 2018). |map=Japan Osaka |map_dot_label=Tsudo Shiroyama
Kofun |type=Keyhole tumulus-SE |architectural_styles={{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} }} [[File:Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, kouenbu-3.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area Sign}}]] '''Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun''' (津堂城山古墳) is a [[:en:Kofun|Kofun]] (ancient Kofun) located in [[:en:Fujiidera|Fujidera City]], [[:en:Osaka Prefecture|Osaka Prefecture]]. It is a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] and part of the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]], which is Historic Site1 as a [[:en:Cultural property|World Historic Site Site]]. While the actual person buried is unknown, the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] has Historic Site1 it as the "'''Fujidera Mausoleum Reference Area'''" and associated it with the 19th Emperor [[:en:Emperor Ingyō|Ingyō Tennō]]. The kofun is also Historic Site1 as a National Historic Site (as part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]"). == Overview == The front of the tumulus faces southeast and is surrounded by a double moat. While the outer moat has been converted into residential and agricultural land, the overall length of the kofun, including the moats, exceeds 400 meters. Excavations indicate that the kofun was built in the late 4th century, making it one of the earliest kofun in the [[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] and predating the {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 誉田御廟山古墳}}. During the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], the site was modified for use as Koyama Castle, resulting in partial excavation of the mound. In the early [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]], the kofun was not Historic Site1 as an imperial tomb. However, in 1912, the excavation of stone slabs from the rear mound for use in shrine construction revealed a vertical stone chamber and a large {{ill|coffer-style Sarcophagus|ja|長持形石棺|1=Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/coffer-style Sarcophagus|13=User:Immanuelle/Chest-shaped Sarcophagus|qq=}}. Numerous burial items, including mirrors and arrowheads, were also discovered. This led to its subsequent Historic Site as the "Fujidera {{ill|Mausoleum Reference Area|ja|陵墓参考地|1=Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum Reference Area|13=User:Immanuelle/Candidate Imperial Mausoleum|qq=}}." Excavations by the Osaka Prefectural Board of Education in 1980 and the Fujidera City Board of Education in 1983 confirmed the presence of plattypes, a double moat (30m inner embankment, 25m outer embankment), and a stone-reinforced outer embankment (20m wide). Island-like features in the moat near the sides of the front mound revealed three waterfowl-shaped [[:en:Haniwa|haniwa]], along with other decorative types such as screens, house types, shields, clothing covers, quivers, and cylindrical haniwa. The construction style, including the multiple moats and embankments, was later adopted in 5th-century imperial tombs like {{ill|Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|lt=Kondoyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kondoyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} and {{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisen Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大仙陵古墳}}. This has led to speculation that Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun represents the origins of such designs and could mark the transition of tomb construction from Yamato to Kawachi, possibly being an early imperial tomb. However, some scholars argue against this interpretation, citing the larger {{ill|Goshajin Kofun|ja|五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|2=ja|3=五社神古墳|4=fr|5=Tombe de Gosashi|6=zh|7=五社神古墳|1=Gosashi Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Goshajin Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gosashi Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} in Saki and contemporary tumuli like {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|lt=Kizuyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kizuyama Kofun|qq=}} and [[:en:Suyama Kofun|Suyama Kofun]] in the Mamigaoka region, which complicate the Historic Site of Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun as an imperial tomb.[[Seike Akira]], *Reevaluating burial Practices in the Kofun built*, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2018, p. 206.{{ill|Yazawa Takatarō|ja|矢澤高太郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yazawa Takatarō|1=Kōtarō Yazawa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11584193}}, *Mausoleums*, Chūōkōron-shinsha, 2012, p. 109. == Cultural designation1 == === National Important designation1 === * Waterfowl-shaped haniwa (three pieces), excavated from Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun, are Historic Site1 as [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Important Cultural Property]] of Japan (Archaeological Material) and housed at {{ill|AICEL Shura Hall|ja|アイセルシュラホール|1=AICEL Shura Hall|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|13=User:Immanuelle/AICEL Shura Hall|qq=}}. Designated on June 9, 2006.{{Historic SiteDB|201|00011241|Haniwa Waterfowl - Osaka Prefecture Shiroyama Kofun}} === National Historic Site === * Shiroyama Kofun is part of the "[[:en:Furuichi Kofun Cluster|Furuichi Kofun Cluster]]" Historic Site, Historic Site1 on January 21, 1958, and expanded in 1966 and 2015.{{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} == Transportation == * [[:en:Minami Osaka Line|Kintetsu Minami-Osaka Line]] [[:en:Fujiidera Station|Fujidera Station]], followed by a [[:en:Kintetsu Bus|Kintetsu Bus]] to Koyama or Taisho Bridge South End (with a subname "Tsudo Shiroyama Kofun-mae"). == References == {{Citations Help}} {{Reflist}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} * {{Historic SiteDB|401|1798|Furuichi Kofun Cluster}} {{Kofun navbar}} {{translated page|ja|津堂城山古墳|version=103415422|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| }} [[ja:津堂城山古墳]] {{Commons category|Tsudo-shiroyama Kofun}} {{wikidata link|Q11555978}} [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Emperor Ingyō]] [[Category:Furuichi Kofun Cluster]] [[Category:History of Fujiidera, Osaka]] [[Category:Important Cultural Property of Japan in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese imperial mausolea (unspecified)]] [[Category:Kofun of Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:National historic sites in Osaka prefecture]] [[Category:pages with conflicting qids]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Zenpokoenfun]]
